decision: Does any matching closed umbrella count as processed, or only one with an explicit accepted/rejected or Steward-receipt disposition?
whyItMatters: The staged implementation suppresses a matching finding even if a human closed it with unresolved rows; the opposite rule can recreate daily issue noise.
evidence: PR #2133 comments 6344218194 and 6344758147 describe competing recreation/suppression behavior and explicitly request a founder ruling.
The staged evidence classifier preserves payload identity, treats contradictory history as unknown, and suppresses a finding when closed history records the same suite, version and candidate ids.
Tests prove that behavior, not its governance validity. The new batch path is not the default scheduled path.

Founder rulings batch 1, 2026-11-06, relayed to the Steward owner (Opus) for #2283 (verbatim): "umbrella is closed = epic is done. Normally, epic done in Gaia means no follow ups. If there are indeed follow ups, this is HIGH PRIORITY for close out. This means it is SIGNAL that something was missed."

Ruling as applied: A closed upstream umbrella is a completed epic: suppress duplicate processing of that batch; a genuinely new version/candidate is new work; unfinished children or contradictory closure evidence are a HIGH-PRIORITY closeout discrepancy (preserve the closure, investigate, reconcile; never fabricate completion).
recommended: A closed upstream umbrella is a completed epic: suppress duplicate processing of that batch; a genuinely new version/candidate is new work; unfinished children or contradictory closure evidence are a HIGH-PRIORITY closeout discrepancy (preserve the closure, investigate, reconcile; never fabricate completion).
alternative: Require a formal receipt or explicit rejection; unresolved human-closed findings then remain actionable and may be recreated.
unblocks: Closed-history semantics independently of canonical open-issue identity or Class A authority.
